styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small gray rock about 2x1 tiles with a tiny green tuft at the left. It has only about 4 lightness steps (a light top, a mid body, a dark underside and a dark edge). Beodeul uses 5-6 per material, and the tree-d43edd reference shows far more variation. It measures 10 visible tones per tile, above tree-1a786c (7) but far below tree-d43edd (29). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. But the body reads as a smooth blob with little per-facet shading, cracks, speckle or grain, so it looks like a sticker rather than a stone shaded one by one. Its dark edge pixels are 40% near-neutral, while both references are at 0%, so the outline is a mix of neutral grey and tinted lines and is not consistently the dark tone of the adjacent material. Overall it is thinner and flatter than the references, and the call is a fail.

That reads as about 4 distinct grey steps, against 5-6 on the reference canopies and trunks. The measured facts are not bad: 10 visible tones per tile is above tree-1a786c (7) but far below tree-d43edd (29), and near-flat coverage is 0%. The dark edge pixels are 40% near-neutral, while both references are 0%. A rock is naturally simpler than a tree, but with the neutral outline and few steps it does not clearly match the Beodeul craft level, and when in doubt it fails.
